title: [CQ-V01] Protected required check definitions
description:
Objective: Define approved check references/digests covering commands, configs, scripts and protected assertion roots.

Deliverable: Protected required check definitions. This is task V01 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): F03.
definitionOfDone: Candidate changes to protected definitions require new approval revision.
Required acceptance overlay is loaded from approved snapshot.
Candidate-added tests cannot silently replace protected required checks.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
The shared delivery predicate enforces protected required checks (packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/policy.ts). It is the one completion and dependency predicate; there is no parallel one.

1. Vocabulary, built only here:
   - EVIDENCE_TOKENS.protectedChecksUnapproved = 'protected-checks-unapproved';
   - EVIDENCE_TOKENS.protectedChecksUnmeasured = 'protected-checks-unmeasured';
   - PROTECTED_CHECK_CHANGED_PREFIX = 'protected-check-changed:', with protectedCheckChangedToken(path).
2. protectedCheckShortfall(state, task):
   - No executionContract.requiredChecks -> [] (unchanged).
   - snapshot = readRequiredCheckSnapshot(task). null -> [protectedChecksUnapproved] (DoD 2: the required acceptance overlay comes ONLY from the approved snapshot, never from candidate data or live settings).
   - current candidate = the last of listCandidatesForTask, the same rule hasPassingCheck uses. If there is none, or it has no protectedEntries -> protectedChecksUnmeasured.
   - Otherwise compare the candidate's entries with snapshot.entries, restricted to paths equal to a protectedPaths() entry or under one followed by '/'. A changed oid, a removed path, or an ADDED path (a candidate-added test under an assertion root, DoD 3) each gives protectedCheckChangedToken(path).
     - Tokens are sorted by path. At most 10, then one 'protected-check-changed:+<n> more'.
     - The path stays held until a new approval revision re-measures it (DoD 1: submit_plan with requiredCheckRevision = the candidate tree).
   - Then, for every APPROVED definition: requiredCheckToken(def.command) unless a CheckRun exists on the current candidate, on its own treeSha, with run.command.trim() === def.command, exitCode 0, source runner-observed. Factor the shared match out of hasPassingCheck, so a candidate-added test command never satisfies a protected one (DoD 3).
   - Error handling: wrap the lookups like hasPassingCheck. A throw is logged and reported as protectedChecksUnmeasured plus the definitions' required-check tokens. Fail closed.
3. evaluateDeliveryEvidence appends protectedCheckShortfall after checkShortfall, de-duplicated in first-seen order: the same command owed by qualityGate appears once.
4. legacy still returns early, unchanged. Update the module header comment on what the check requirement now covers.

Consumers read the same verdict.
- state/deliveryProjection.ts:
  - checkOwed is also true when the task's contract has requiredChecks.
  - requiredCheckSatisfiedFor returns false when any missing token starts with 'protected-check' (both the plural protected-checks-* tokens and the protected-check-changed: prefix), alongside the existing required-check rule.
  This way JetBrains/VS Code never show a satisfied check while protected checks drifted. The client display wording stays as it is; the CQ-V12 sweep owns the docs.
- tools/getContext.ts (next to executionContract, ~422): serve `requiredCheckSnapshot: readRequiredCheckSnapshot(task)` to every role, only when it is non-null. This is the overlay source a runner loads: the protected files at `revision`. A stale or forged snapshot is never served.
- Error handling: a malformed stored snapshot is omitted, never thrown into get_context.

DoD-level tests in a new file, packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts.
Use ToolTestHarness with settings.deliveryPolicy 'local-branch': non-legacy and evaluated today, with no verified-local needed. Seed the snapshot through V01b's submit_plan path on a temporary git repo if its helper is exported; otherwise seed the daemon-owned field directly in harness state, with definitionDigest(defs) computed by the landed helper. Assert exact missingEvidence arrays with toEqual.
(a) Match: candidate entries equal to the snapshot, plus a passing runner-observed run of each approved command on the candidate tree -> no protected token.
(b) DoD 1:
  - a changed oid gives protected-check-changed:<path>;
  - a removed file gives its token;
  - after a NEW approval revision whose snapshot equals the candidate's entries, the tokens clear.
(c) DoD 3:
  - a test file added under an assertion root gives its token;
  - a passing run of a different, candidate-added command leaves required-check:<approved command> missing.
(d) DoD 2:
  - the contract's requiredChecks changed through updateTask without resubmission (digest mismatch) gives protected-checks-unapproved;
  - get_context serves requiredCheckSnapshot to worker and QA only while it is valid.
(e) A candidate without protectedEntries gives protected-checks-unmeasured.
(f) A legacy deliveryPolicy, and a task without requiredChecks, are unchanged: no protected tokens, and deliveryProjection omits or keeps today's values.
(g) Shared predicate: a dependent of a drifted task is withheld by the dependency gate, and deliveryProjection.requiredCheckSatisfied is false on drift and true on a match.
Run `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/delivery/requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts` while iterating.

Verification gate (run once, fresh).
This changes a shared wire shape (Candidate, the delivery tokens, get_context), so run the full suite:
- NAMED COMMAND: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test`, plus `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- Run them where node_modules matches the OS, per the epic note: on Linux use a separate native dependency install with unchanged lockfile and source hashes, and never overwrite the Windows node_modules. Use a Linux-only PATH, with MOE_* unset.
- Supply the npm test output to complete_task.
A failure outside this task's files must be shown to fail on a clean `git archive HEAD` snapshot before you call it pre-existing.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Split by SPIDR into V01a (shape), V01b (daemon-measured snapshot) and V01 (this final slice). The full feature is about 900 lines, and QA rejects anything over 400 net. V01 keeps its human-owned DoD and proves it end to end.

Rejected:
- Daemon git reads of candidate trees. record_candidate's documented contract is 'never checked against git', and isolated VM runners' trees need not exist in the host repo. The runner reports protectedEntries instead, and V03 authenticates it.
- Per-file raw-bytes hashing. It would disagree with git's EOL normalization (the b62c9fc7 lesson). Git object ids on both sides compare exactly.
- A second completion predicate. The epic demands one shared predicate, so tokens flow through evaluateDeliveryEvidence.
- Overlay execution, i.e. running checks with protected files restored. That is V04 (frozen focused check dispatch). V01 only names the overlay source and enforces it in the predicate.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
delivery/policy.ts: evaluateDeliveryEvidence. legacy returns early; checkShortfall and hasPassingCheck pick the current candidate as the last by createdAt then id, and use runner-observed exit-0 runs on the candidate tree. Its tokens are consumed by qa_approve, the dependency gate and deliveryProjection.

state/candidateStore.ts: validateCandidateParams refuses rather than coerces; replayOrRefuse compares the RECORDED_FIELDS scalars, so arrays need a deep compare. tools/recordCandidate.ts: inputSchema has additionalProperties false.

state/deliveryProjection.ts: checkOwed and requiredCheckSatisfiedFor (~66-82). tools/getContext.ts: executionContract projection at ~422.

The settings.deliveryPolicy 'local-branch' path is evaluated today without verified-local, which makes tests possible. Strict execution-profile tasks throw until verified-local is certified.
planningNotes.risks:
- V01a and V01b are unlanded at plan time. Step 1 makes the worker follow the landed names.
- candidateStore.ts is contested by the stale task-07474ee4 until c2cb5cf7 lands, so edit it with Edit/Write.
- Under a non-legacy deliveryPolicy, a task with requiredChecks now blocks QA approval and dependents until its protected checks pass. That is intended; legacy projects are unaffected.
- Token-list growth is capped at 10 changed paths plus a summary.
- The client projections now read false for protected drift. JetBrains/VS Code wording and the docs are held for CQ-V12.
